neighborhoods.name: Downtown Hagåtña
neighborhoods.description: Guam's small historic capital district, laid out in walkable city blocks around Chamorro Village, the Guam Museum, Paseo de Susana park, and government offices
neighborhoods.character: Historic, civic, walkable core, small-scale, waterfront
neighborhoods.character_notes: The most walkable address on Guam: banks, courts, churches, the Agana Shopping Center, and the Chamorro Village night market are within a flat, compact grid, and Hagåtña is the hub of GRTA's limited bus network. You will still want a car for big-box shopping and medical specialists; Guam Memorial Hospital in Tamuning is about 10 minutes away. Rental stock is limited, and military housing-allowance demand supports rents above Dededo levels.

neighborhoods.name: Anigua
neighborhoods.description: Residential western edge of Hagåtña along Marine Corps Drive, denser with homes than the civic downtown and a short hop to both the capital and Tamuning
neighborhoods.character: Residential, central, unpretentious, roadside commercial strip

housing.predominantType: Concrete single-family homes and small apartment buildings

neighborhoods.character_notes: A practical, slightly cheaper alternative to downtown with quick car access along Marine Corps Drive to Guam Memorial Hospital (under 10 minutes) and Tamuning shopping. Sidewalks are patchy and the main road is busy, so day-to-day errands still mean driving. Housing is mostly typhoon-rated concrete, and GRTA routes passing through to the Hagåtña hub give it slightly better bus access than outlying villages.

neighborhoods.name: Agana Heights
neighborhoods.description: Elevated residential village on the cliffline directly above Hagåtña, home to U.S. Naval Hospital Guam and prized for its ocean views and cooler breezes
neighborhoods.character: Hillside, view homes, well-kept, military-professional, quiet

housing.predominantType: Single-family view homes and cliffside condos

neighborhoods.character_notes: A standout for retirees who prioritize healthcare access: U.S. Naval Hospital Guam is inside the village and Guam Memorial Hospital is a 10-15 minute drive. Cliffside condo buildings offer elevators and ocean views, but the hilly terrain means nothing is realistically walkable and a car is required. One of Guam's safer, better-kept villages, with rents at the top of the capital-area range.

neighborhoods.name: Sinajana
neighborhoods.description: Small, tight-knit residential village on the hills immediately southeast of Hagåtña, one of Guam's most densely settled but lowest-key communities
neighborhoods.character: Village feel, tight-knit, affordable, hillside, local
neighborhoods.character_notes: The budget option in the capital area: quiet streets, a strong neighborhood identity, and small apartment units near the village center (some walkable to a Payless Supermarket). It is still car-dependent for everything else, with downtown Hagåtña 5 minutes and Guam Memorial Hospital about 15 minutes by car. Modest single-story concrete homes are the norm, which works well for aging in place and typhoon resilience.
